question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2w+3}+1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2w+3}+1,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{w+1}{\sqrt{2w+3}-1} & = \\ \frac{w+1}{\sqrt{2w+3}-1}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2w+3}+1}{\sqrt{2w+3}+1} & = \\ \frac{(w+1)(\sqrt{2w+3}+1)}{(\sqrt{2w+3}-1)(\sqrt{2w+3}+1)} & = \\ \frac{(w+1)(\sqrt{2w+3}+1)}{(\sqrt{2w+3})^{2}-{1}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{(w+1)(\sqrt{2w+3}+1)}{2w+3-1} & = \\ \frac{(w+1)(\sqrt{2w+3}+1)}{2w+2} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{(w+1)}(\sqrt{2w+3}+1)}{2\cancel{(w+1)}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2w+3}+1}{2} & \end{aligned}
$$
